title: Our Solar System
summary: Meet the Sun and its eight planets, and see how they travel around it.

steps.title: The Sun is our star
sentences: The Sun is a giant ball of hot, glowing gas.
It is a star, just like the tiny lights you see at night.
The Sun gives us light and warmth, and everything in our Solar System travels around it.

steps.title: Eight planets
sentences: There are eight planets that go around the Sun.
In order from the Sun they are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
The path a planet takes around the Sun is called its orbit.
points: A planet's path is an orbit

steps.title: Small and big
sentences: The four planets nearest the Sun are small and rocky, and Earth is one of them.
The four planets farther away are huge and are made mostly of gas and ice.
Jupiter is the biggest planet of all.
points: Near the Sun: small and rocky
Far from the Sun: huge and gassy

steps.title: A year is a trip
sentences: One trip around the Sun is called a year.
Earth takes about 365 days to make one trip.
Mercury is close to the Sun, so it finishes a trip in only 88 days, but Neptune takes about 165 Earth years.

facts: If the Sun were a large front door, Earth would be about the size of a coin.
Saturn is so light for its size that, on average, it is less dense than water.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.

quiz.why: Jupiter is the biggest planet, more than 1,000 Earths could fit inside it.

quiz.q: What do we call the path a planet takes around the Sun?
quiz.why: The curved path of a planet around the Sun is called its orbit.

quiz.q: How many planets are in our Solar System?
quiz.why: There are eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

notes: The IAU defined 'planet' in 2006, which is why Pluto is now called a dwarf planet.
